6:04 - In all my years… this is one thing I have never quite understood. To be fair, there are some circumstances where I can see it happening, like in the first few months when the parents are trying to get used to a new routine and they are a bit sleep deprived. I have seen a night camera footage of a woman who had already put the baby down for the night and she made the gesture to lay them down. That… I can understand because when you are that tired… you are very spacey, swearing up and down you didn’t do something when you actually had already done it. Two days before.

But when the baby is a toddler? You had that routine down for roughly a year and a half. The baby has been in the car almost every single day. I have never met a parent who wasn’t hyper vigilant by this point (the year that this baby died. There was a time when I was still in high school where it seemed as if a baby was left in a car every day for a week. No, I am not exaggerating. I swear it was like one baby a day all across the country. It was pretty bad that they did a news report on how to be vigilant). Also.. he has done this multiple times! If this is the case I am thinking of… the mother came home and said: “I told you to stop leaving her in the car!” 

I’m not going to lie. People were angry as heck towards that mother. The talking points went from that father’s evil to the mother and asking the question: “He has done this a few times before… why are you leaving your child with him!?” I’m sure the mother was broken hearted but a part of you has to wonder: why hadn’t she left him after the second time? Why did she continue to leave her daughter with someone that irresponsible? 

Side Story: I read this Reddit story about this young mother who was working I believe and every time she came home her baby was changed and fed, but her neighbor asked her if something was wrong because one day her baby was crying for hours. She thought that was weird so she set it up where she came home earlier than usual. Slipping into the house, she found the kitchen wrecked, her baby screaming and her son covered in all kinds of stuff. He apologized because the baby had started to cry and he knew to make her milk but hadn’t learned how (he was really young) so he attempted to feed her chips but the baby only cried harder.

Her scum of a husband had locked himself in their room with earplugs in his ears! And would only wake up right before the mother came home and do everything that she expected him to have done. She left him that very day.

Edit to Add: Both of my parents were very negligent when I was younger from what I’ve heard from their own lips and from my memory, it is very surprising that I made it to 43. 

1. Left in a sink full of soapy water - This happened when I was almost a year old. My mother claimed that she had received a phone call and left me unattended in the sink where she had been giving me a bath. She also claimed that she left me in the sink no more than a few seconds and when she returned, she couldn’t see me and thought I had drowned. When she got closer to the sink, she saw my little hand wrapped around the faucet and when she pulled me out of the water she found I had closed my eyes tightly and my cheeks were puffed with air. I refused to open my eyes or breathe until she squeezed my cheeks. This was attributed to me being intelligent. I wonder how often she had left me in the sink for me to know water was dangerous.

2. Sleep til 12 pm: My mother would proudly tell the story of how, as a baby, I would wake up early but not make a sound for hours. And I do mean hours until she would wake up at 12 PM. When she did, I would ask if it was time to wake up. I was often left in my crib with no food, no drink, and a diaper full. I insisted that knowing the type of parent she was… she must have screamed at me to not wake her. She was not sleep deprived by the way, I was told I never cried even when hungry or wet.

3. Was in a pool at 3 or 4 - My dad and his friends wanted to go swimming but I was at home and his mother was at work. Before my grandmother left, she always made sure I was dressed, fed breakfast, and kept entertained. Usually, I was left alone in her room with the door locked since she couldn’t trust my dad. When I was allowed to do this, I didn’t leave the room at all. On this day, however, I was out and they decided to go to the YMCA. I don’t believe I wore a bathing suit but I was given a life preserver because I had not been taught to swim. I stretched out my arms and slipped through the ring. A cousin saw I was missing and disappeared under the water to get me. Again I had held my breath so no water entered my lungs. My dad begged me not to say anything. Told on him the moment my grandmother returned home. Dad was banned from ever leaving the house with me and if it was an emergency, he was to take me to a neighbor’s home. 

4. Lost at Great America (the first time) - Thanks to my grandmother’s employment, she was given gifts by the families of patients she looked after and always had season passes to Great America. That summer was with the extended family and had walked up to the map to see what rides the kids could get on and where they were located. I pointed at the map and told my dad I would like to get on some ride and turned around to find myself - alone. Everyone had disappeared on me. That was three adults and a gaggle of children. I wondered through the park trying to find them. Was found by a young couple from West Virginia (they told me and I never forgot). They took me on a ride or two and thought my family had abandoned me. A few weekends before two children had been dumped at the same Great America so they believed that happened to me. They kept me entertained, keeping an eye out for my family… but couldn’t locate anyone. At the time there wasn’t an area where children could be sent when separated from family. They discussed what they should do with me; talked about where I could sleep, that I would need all new furniture, all new clothes, that there were really good schools where they lived, the works. This was being decided after they said they would take me to the police and keep an ear out for me in case I truly had been abandoned and they would adopt me. I eventually lied and said I saw my family and had to go. I even waved so they thought I had found my family. I never got creepy vibes from them. Were very young in their 20s and very kind to a strange child. Did find my family a few minutes later. Was blamed. Went home, told on my dad and the extended family. From then on Dad was never allowed to take me anywhere and this time… it stuck.

After that adventure, I often left my family, explored the park (yes, alone) and road on rides. I was never bothered by anyone and did not ended up snatched. Still amazed at that. 

People… please be sure to keep your eyes on your child at all times. I know it’s pretty hard because children disappear in seconds, just stay vigilant.

Bonus Story: I left my kindergarten school to visit my cousin at her elementary school. In my little four year old brain, the schools weren’t’ that far apart. They were. Was found by a teacher who was bringing her class back from a walk. She held my hand, escorted me back to school where everyone was having recess. My hand was held by a yard supervisor for the rest of recess. I hated that. I don’t remember if my grandmother was told and I actually told her a few days later. She was flabbergasted and upset. But then again, she knew me as the child who would ditch my family at an amusement park and go off on my lonesome and the child who would walk around our local mall to visit all of the shops and security. 

Again… I was never bothered when I walked around the mall because I was so famous for doing this that every employee and security guard would watch over me. I remember one mother being especially concerned about my safety and reported that she saw a little black girl walking around the mall without her parents. The guard informed her that they all knew me and kept a tight watch over me. I had often heard them talking on their walkie talkies to each other to acknowledge that they saw me and where I was headed and as soon as someone saw me, they would tell the others. They knew me by name and my mother was always in the same store anyway. 

I even was something of an honorary cashier as whenever I visited the employees could have a bathroom break and I would sit behind the register to wait for customers. A woman walked in and her mouth fell open seeing me calmly sitting behind the register. I informed her that the employee would be right out since she had to use the bathroom. Less than a minute later the cashier appeared and thanked me. The customer asked if I was her little sister and she shook her head saying that I was the mall’s child. I had full permission from the security guards and the store owners of the various shops to come and go as I pleased and if an employee had to use it… I was the only one allowed behind the register because I didn’t touch anything. Would just sit down on the stool and wait for customers.
